headline: Costco beat EPS estimates with sales up 11%, helped by gas inflation and a one-time tariff refund, and keeps reinvesting in price.

metrics.comp_label: Costco U.S. comp ex gas & FX

guidance_note: Costco does not give earnings guidance. EPS of $6.75 includes a $0.15 nonrecurring IEEPA tariff-refund benefit (~$6.60 excluding it).
key_messages: U.S. comps +10.7% reported, +7.2% ex gas and FX; total company +9.4% / +6.7% adjusted. Gas inflation added ~3 pts.
Worldwide traffic +3.3%, ticket +5.9% (+3.3% ex gas/FX); digitally enabled comps +19.5%.
Membership fee income $1.85B (+7.3%); U.S./Canada renewal 92.3%, worldwide 89.8%, both up 10 bps.
Received $184M in tariff refunds and is reinvesting most into lower prices (e.g., Kirkland coffee, walnuts).
LIFO charge of $152M tied to memory-chip costs in electronics and Middle East-related gas/resin inflation.

consumer.big_ticket: Growth spread across meat, bakery, majors, electronics and health & beauty.
consumer.pricing: Inflation in gas, electronics (memory) and resins; tariff refunds reinvested in lower member prices.

macro_read: Members kept shopping more often and spending more, though gas-price inflation inflates headline sales; demand at Costco remains healthy into fall 2026.

sources.label: Fox Business: Costco receives $184M in tariff refunds

notes: EPS of $6.75 includes a $0.15 one-time tariff-refund benefit; about $6.60 without it. The beat is measured on $6.60.
